### Reading the batch tables

Batch rows from every sub-campaign share one table per route; the `module` cell names the
row's sub-campaign as `<link-unit>/<module>`, the same name as its Overview row.
Every type row is a `wrap` batch: the rows the wrap campaign landed, kept in the `Types`
tables' `objective` column since the template merged its wrap and port tables. A `wavefront` report category, for ownership findings the review resubmitted, is
counted under `+misc`.

Each batch is measured on two tree states: just before its first landing commit (the wave
base or the previous batch's landing) and its last landing commit. `cov (C/Rust)` is the
latter, from one instrumented build per state: the four workloads (`--lib` unit tests,
`ub_safe`, `ub_unsafe`, `equiv`) each run alone into their own profile directory against
the `coverage` prebuild, and their union is the cell. C is lcov line coverage over the 196
translation units `libgit2.so` links, with a zero baseline from the `.gcno` files so that
untouched TUs count; Rust is cargo-llvm-cov line coverage over `crustify/rust/libgit2`'s
non-`tests/` sources, minus every line inside a `#[cfg(test)]` item (the inline unit-test
modules). All workloads share one denominator, and the union is the union of their covered
lines. Every Rust cell and Rust delta in these tables was restated on 2026-10-12. The
earlier figures counted those test lines, 60% of the instrumented lines at the
`libgit2/index` tip, which held the integration suites' coverage far down and credited
the unit tests for running themselves. All 182 recorded states were re-measured; the C
cells and C deltas stay as first recorded. The eight `libgit2/config` states between
`beeda6a07` and the export revert `c5440d3ee` call the two reverted constructors, so they
were measured against a private coverage build of their own source, which exports them. A Σ `cov` cell is the state after the table's chronologically
last landing. The `(+C/+Rust pp)` pairs in the `…: tests` tables are each workload's own
coverage after minus before, so a batch that adds code its workload does not reach shows a
negative Rust delta. The safety audit deltas are the Safety audit's metrics over the same two
states, from the scans the `ffimap` skill names; the tables hold no row from before the
metrics were redefined, as `Safety audit metrics from ffimap's counter tree` describes.

Test counts are `#[test]` functions the landing commits add, by directory; trybuild
`compile_fail` cases are not counted. `+LoC` and `rv loc` count `.rs` lines under
`crustify/rust/`, so review reproducer crates under `crustify/reviews/` are excluded. The
measurement scripts live outside the repository, beside the orchestrator's other helpers;
each batch's `ffimap.json` beside it is the unseeded scan of its last landing commit.

### Overview test counts

The Coverage stats test lines were measured again on 2026-11-04, at `crustify/devel`
`1e732ebff`, with the testing spec's Coverage method, which replaces the gcov one the
earlier figures used. Those figures are not comparable with these. Each count is the
number of tests its compiled test binary registers (`-- --list`): `--lib` for the unit
tests, one of them ignored, and the `ub_safe`, `ub_unsafe` and `equiv` integration crates.
The trybuild runner is one `ub_safe` test, and it was skipped in the coverage run since it
runs no code. `ub_safe` holds 688 tests since the unsafe fixtures were removed. Doctests
are not counted in the table.

The `coverage` variant, `build.json` version 4, and the side libraries' `coverage`
installs (version 3 of each) compile the C with clang 23,
`-fprofile-instr-generate -fcoverage-mapping`. The Rust is a scratch copy under
`crustify/tmp/coverage/` with `#[coverage(off)]` on every test item, compiled on
`nightly-2026-10-08` (LLVM 23) with `-C instrument-coverage`. Each suite ran alone into
its own profile, and `Total tests` is the merge of the four suites' profiles, their union.
Every figure is the `TOTAL` line of the nightly's `llvm-cov report`, with `libgit2.so` and
every test binary as objects for every suite.

- C is line coverage over the 86,770 lines `libgit2.so` maps to `c/src/libgit2`,
  `c/src/util`, `c/include` and the bundled `c/deps` it compiles (`llhttp`, `ntlmclient`,
  `reftable`, `xdiff`). The generated headers and the C's own tests count toward none.
  libgit2 proper, `src/` and `include/` without `deps/`, is `52.42`% of 68,023 lines. The
  total covers `61.63`% of functions and `47.65`% of regions.
- Rust is line coverage over the 13,226 lines of the crate's 42 files under `src/`, with
  `tests/`, the `-sys` crate and dependencies left out by path. The total covers `99.02`% of
  functions and `97.65`% of regions.
- Doctests, run as a suite of their own: 347, of which 346 pass under the nightly. The
  compile-fail doctest on `CommitBuilder` expects `E0624`, which stable reports and the
  nightly does not; it passes on plain. They reach `11.94`% of C lines and `23.30`% of
  Rust lines, and add no line to the four suites' union.

`crustify/scripts/coverage/` holds the scripts that measured them:
`run.sh "$PWD" libgit2 "$PWD/crustify/tmp/coverage"`, then
`report.py crustify/tmp/coverage "C=$PWD/c/src/libgit2:$PWD/c/src/util:$PWD/c/include:$PWD/c/deps,Rust=$PWD/crustify/tmp/coverage/tree/src" --c crustify/builds/coverage/libgit2.so.1.9.0`.

The UB suites also run under ASan+UBSan, TSan, Miri and BorrowSanitizer in the agents'
gates. Those runs share one test set and are not counted again.

### Batches — review: PoC + reports
### Reading the batch tables

Batch rows from every sub-campaign share one table per route; the `module` cell names the
row's sub-campaign as `<link-unit>/<module>`, the same name as its Overview row.
Every type row is a `wrap` batch: the rows the wrap campaign landed, kept in the `Types`
tables' `objective` column since the template merged its wrap and port tables. A `wavefront` report category, for ownership findings the review resubmitted, is
counted under `+misc`.

Each batch is measured on two tree states: just before its first landing commit (the wave
base or the previous batch's landing) and its last landing commit. `cov (C/Rust)` is the
latter, from one instrumented build per state: the four workloads (`--lib` unit tests,
`ub_safe`, `ub_unsafe`, `equiv`) each run alone into their own profile directory against
the `coverage` prebuild, and their union is the cell. C is lcov line coverage over the 196
translation units `libgit2.so` links, with a zero baseline from the `.gcno` files so that
untouched TUs count; Rust is cargo-llvm-cov line coverage over `crustify/rust/libgit2`'s
non-`tests/` sources, minus every line inside a `#[cfg(test)]` item (the inline unit-test
modules). All workloads share one denominator, and the union is the union of their covered
lines. Every Rust cell and Rust delta in these tables was restated on 2026-10-12. The
earlier figures counted those test lines, 60% of the instrumented lines at the
`libgit2/index` tip, which held the integration suites' coverage far down and credited
the unit tests for running themselves. All 182 recorded states were re-measured; the C
cells and C deltas stay as first recorded. The eight `libgit2/config` states between
`beeda6a07` and the export revert `c5440d3ee` call the two reverted constructors, so they
were measured against a private coverage build of their own source, which exports them. A Σ `cov` cell is the state after the table's chronologically
last landing. The `(+C/+Rust pp)` pairs in the `…: tests` tables are each workload's own
coverage after minus before, so a batch that adds code its workload does not reach shows a
negative Rust delta. The safety audit deltas are the Safety audit's metrics over the same two
states, from the scans the `ffimap` skill names; the tables hold no row from before the
metrics were redefined, as `Safety audit metrics from ffimap's counter tree` describes.

Test counts are `#[test]` functions the landing commits add, by directory; trybuild
`compile_fail` cases are not counted. `+LoC` and `rv loc` count `.rs` lines under
`crustify/rust/`, so review reproducer crates under `crustify/reviews/` are excluded. The
measurement scripts live outside the repository, beside the orchestrator's other helpers;
each batch's `ffimap.json` beside it is the unseeded scan of its last landing commit.

### Overview test counts

The Coverage stats test lines were measured again on 2026-11-04, at `crustify/devel`
`1e732ebff`, with the testing spec's Coverage method, which replaces the gcov one the
earlier figures used. Those figures are not comparable with these. Each count is the
number of tests its compiled test binary registers (`-- --list`): `--lib` for the unit
tests, one of them ignored, and the `ub_safe`, `ub_unsafe` and `equiv` integration crates.
The trybuild runner is one `ub_safe` test, and it was skipped in the coverage run since it
runs no code. `ub_safe` holds 688 tests since the unsafe fixtures were removed. Doctests
are not counted in the table.

The `coverage` variant, `build.json` version 4, and the side libraries' `coverage`
installs (version 3 of each) compile the C with clang 23,
`-fprofile-instr-generate -fcoverage-mapping`. The Rust is a scratch copy under
`crustify/tmp/coverage/` with `#[coverage(off)]` on every test item, compiled on
`nightly-2026-10-08` (LLVM 23) with `-C instrument-coverage`. Each suite ran alone into
its own profile, and `Total tests` is the merge of the four suites' profiles, their union.
Every figure is the `TOTAL` line of the nightly's `llvm-cov report`, with `libgit2.so` and
every test binary as objects for every suite.

- C is line coverage over the 86,770 lines `libgit2.so` maps to `c/src/libgit2`,
  `c/src/util`, `c/include` and the bundled `c/deps` it compiles (`llhttp`, `ntlmclient`,
  `reftable`, `xdiff`). The generated headers and the C's own tests count toward none.
  libgit2 proper, `src/` and `include/` without `deps/`, is `52.42`% of 68,023 lines. The
  total covers `61.63`% of functions and `47.65`% of regions.
- Rust is line coverage over the 13,226 lines of the crate's 42 files under `src/`, with
  `tests/`, the `-sys` crate and dependencies left out by path. The total covers `99.02`% of
  functions and `97.65`% of regions.
- Doctests, run as a suite of their own: 347, of which 346 pass under the nightly. The
  compile-fail doctest on `CommitBuilder` expects `E0624`, which stable reports and the
  nightly does not; it passes on plain. They reach `11.94`% of C lines and `23.30`% of
  Rust lines, and add no line to the four suites' union.

`crustify/scripts/coverage/` holds the scripts that measured them:
`run.sh "$PWD" libgit2 "$PWD/crustify/tmp/coverage"`, then
`report.py crustify/tmp/coverage "C=$PWD/c/src/libgit2:$PWD/c/src/util:$PWD/c/include:$PWD/c/deps,Rust=$PWD/crustify/tmp/coverage/tree/src" --c crustify/builds/coverage/libgit2.so.1.9.0`.

The UB suites also run under ASan+UBSan, TSan, Miri and BorrowSanitizer in the agents'
gates. Those runs share one test set and are not counted again.

### `libgit2/deps/ntlmclient/compat.h` wave 200 batch 0: `MIN`

`deps/ntlmclient/compat.h` is a header with no translation unit, and its one scheduled item is
`#define MIN(x, y) (((x) < (y)) ? (x) : (y))`, under `#ifndef MIN`; the header's `bool`,
`true` and `false` are defined only under `_MSC_VER`. `mac::MIN` is the native
`fn min<T: PartialOrd>(x: T, y: T) -> T` in `src/libgit2/deps/ntlmclient/compat_h.rs`, the
macro's body over any `PartialOrd` type: ties and pairs `<` cannot order return `y`, as the C
does, and for an `Ord` type the result is `core::cmp::min`'s, the plan's `rust_equivalent`. It
is not a `const fn`, since a generic comparison cannot be called in a constant on stable Rust
1.100. Its docs name where it departs from the macro: one operand type rather than the usual
arithmetic conversions, and each operand evaluated once, where the macro evaluates the one
it returns twice; `ntlm.c`'s three uses pass `size_t` operands without side effects. The file
holds no unsafe region and carries `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`. No C reaches it and the macro has
no export: it stays in its header for `ntlm.c`'s `des_key_from_password` and
`generate_lm_hash`, wavefront's only users of it. The `loc` cell is wavefront's, `0` for a
macro.

Tests: six `unit_pub` tests (`ntlm.c`'s key-length uses for every password length up to 20,
integers of each width at their bounds against `Ord::min`, which operand a tie returns, NaN and
signed zeros, single evaluation of each operand, and owned operands), and a doctest. No `equiv`
test: the macro's C users are static functions of `ntlm.c`, reached only through
`ntlm_client_response`, which the raw bindings do not reach and no suite calls (`ntlm.c` is at
`0.00`% of its 967 lines in every suite), and binding `deps/ntlmclient/ntlm.h` is `ntlm.c`'s
batches'. The module has no C tests to carry over.

Coverage was measured with `crustify/scripts/coverage/run.sh` on a `git archive` of the wave
tip `2216b0cd0` and on this tree, each suite alone, and read with `report.py` from each scratch
tree's `src/libgit2` (`C=@c` over the `coverage` variant's `libcrustify.a`, 89,080 lines, and
Rust over the scratch tree's `src/`), the unit column merging `lib` and `unit_pub`. The tip
measures `44.97`% / `98.81`% in total, where `45.02`% was recorded; the pp cells are against this
run's own tip measurement, and the C shifts, which no test of this batch reaches, are
run-to-run variation. Worklist: Rust `compat_h.rs` 3 of 3 lines, 5 of 5 regions and 1 of 1
function, all by `unit_pub`; the C expansions in `ntlm.c` are reached by no suite. The Overview's
Rust LoC moves by ffimap's `code.loc.total` (`+3`) and `code.tests.loc.total` (`+89`).

The safety audit scans (ffimap `9aa2ef1`, `--ffibox`, `--sys-crates pcre2_sys`, the 13 seams,
`--regions ffi_import,ffi_export`, no export feature: the module has no translation unit) move
only the line and function totals; the boundary scan's sites hold none in the changeset.
`ffimap api` against the tip, with ffibox's private rustdoc JSON (nightly `2026-10-08`):
`mac::MIN` is `new`, and every unattributed module `kept`.

Gates, on the base `2216b0cd0`: the workspace is formatted, and `clippy --workspace
--all-targets` passes with warnings denied on `plain`. The whole workspace passes on `plain`
(`lib` 840 and 1 ignored, `ub_safe` 762, `ub_unsafe` 120, `equiv` 528, `unit_pub` 73,
`hidden_symbols` 1, doctests 73 merged and 378 standalone). The module's six tests and its
doctest pass under ASan+UBSan and under Miri. The coverage runs ran every suite of both trees on
the nightly; only the known `CommitBuilder` compile-fail doctest fails, on both. TSan and BSan
have no obligation: the batch adds no unsafe code, no `Send` or `Sync` claim and no thread. No
raw binding or C changed, so the packaging gate does not apply. Usage cells are the assistant's.
EOF

content.content:
# A macro whose configured branches compute one result is ported once

Status: `open`.

## Signal

A rule an agent had to work out by hand that a skill should have stated.

## Evidence

`wave-225/batch-0/run-1` ported `mac::p_strnlen` (`src/util/strnlen.h`). The header defines
it by platform: `#define p_strnlen strnlen` (libc's), or, under `NO_STRNLEN` (MinGW, Solaris,
Apple, MidnightBSD, old MSVC), a `GIT_INLINE` body over `memchr(s, 0, maxlen)`. Both give
the offset of the first NUL within `maxlen`, or `maxlen`, for every input.

`binding-symbols`' Macros section reaches "a macro whose expansion depends on the build's
configuration" through a shim, `crustify_<NAME>`, and binds a symbol alias "through the safe
wrapper of the symbol it names". `porting-symbols`' Macros section defers to it. Read
literally, the port would be a shim over libc's `strnlen`, or a wrapper of it, though
`dependencies.json` gives libc's `strnlen` the `std` route and nothing of its state is
shared with C. The task message had to settle it: "Port what this build defines, and say in
its docs what the other branch is." The batch ported a native `const fn strnlen(&[u8])`, by
`CStr::from_bytes_until_nul`, and documented the `NO_STRNLEN` branch on it.

The module pass, `wave-225/batch-1/run-1`, judged the port against `porting-symbols`'
Macros section and filed no finding: the body computes on its arguments alone, so it takes
the `const` function form, and libc's `strnlen` is reached by its `std` route. The reading
the shim exception invites is unclear twice over: what selects the branch here is the
target platform (`__APPLE__`, `__sun`, `__MINGW32__`, `__MidnightBSD__`, `_MSC_VER`), which
Rust's own `cfg(target_os, target_env)` does see, and a port reimplements the body instead
of reaching the C's expansion, so a shim over the C would make the port a binding. The
section should say which configurations the exception means, and that it applies only
where the branches differ in what they compute.

## Destination

The spec: `porting-symbols`' Macros section.

## Change

Add, after its first paragraph:

> A macro whose expansion depends on the build's configuration is ported once when every
> configuration's expansion computes the same result for every input, its documentation
> naming the branches the build does not take; only one whose branches differ in what they
> compute keeps `binding-symbols`' shim. A symbol alias of an out-of-tree library's entity
> is ported as that entity's route reaches it, as `dependencies`' Confirmation section
> checks it: through the standard library, it is a native function.

## Validation

`wave-225/batch-0`'s tests: its unit tests check every NUL position in every bound up to 70
bytes against the standard library's scan, and its equivalence tests compare the port with
the C's expansion, glibc's `strnlen`, through `git__strndup`. The `NO_STRNLEN` branch is
not built on this host; its body is the same scan by reading.

# A macro that evaluates an operand twice only as a hazard is a function

Status: `open`.

## Signal

A rule an agent had to work out by hand that a skill should have stated.

## Evidence

`wave-200/batch-0/run-1` ported `mac::MIN` (`deps/ntlmclient/compat.h`),
`#define MIN(x, y) (((x) < (y)) ? (x) : (y))`. The expansion evaluates the operand it
returns twice and the other once.

`binding-symbols`' Macros section, which `porting-symbols`' Macros section defers to, gives a
macro that implements logic a function, and lets a `macro_rules!` take its place "only where
a function cannot express it: control flow that leaves its caller, token pasting or
stringification, an argument used as a place, or one evaluated lazily or more than once."
Read literally, `MIN` is such a macro, and so is every C `MIN`, `MAX`, `ABS` or `CLAMP` macro of
the usual form: its operand is evaluated more than once. Yet no caller relies on that: the
double evaluation is the classic hazard of such macros, not their meaning, and `ntlm.c`'s
three uses pass operands without side effects, whose result is the same whether they are
evaluated once or twice. A `macro_rules!` copying the double evaluation would carry the
hazard into Rust and lose the function's type checking. The batch ported a generic
`fn min<T: PartialOrd>(x: T, y: T) -> T`, documenting the departure, and decided the
reading by hand.

The rule's exception is right for a macro whose callers observe the repeated or lazy
evaluation: one that re-reads an argument it also writes, or evaluates an argument only on
one branch, as an `assert`- or `likely`-style macro, or a short-circuiting one, does. It
needs to say that the evaluation counts only where a caller depends on it.

## Destination

The spec: `porting-symbols`' Macros section, which this role evolves; `binding-symbols`'
Macros section states the same exception for a binding, whose owner may take the same
sentence.

## Change

Add to `porting-symbols`' Macros section, after its first sentence:

> An argument the expansion evaluates lazily or more than once calls for a `macro_rules!`
> only where a caller depends on it: where every expansion site passes an argument without
> side effects, whose result is the same evaluated once, the macro is a function, its
> documentation naming the difference, as a `MIN` or `MAX` of the usual form is.

## Validation

`wave-200/batch-0`'s tests: six `unit_pub` tests check the function against the macro's body,
`ntlm.c`'s three uses for every password length up to 20, ties, unordered floats, and that each
operand is evaluated once. The expansion sites were read in `ntlm.c` (lines 953, 987 and 988),
and wavefront's `query macros --name MIN` lists no other user of the header's macro.

## Review

None yet.
EOF

Its body is the macro's own ternary, so a tie or a NaN returns `y` just as the C does. For integer and other `Ord` types it gives the same result as `core::cmp::min`, which is the standard equivalent the plan names. The file has no unsafe code (`#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`) and no export. The macro stays in its header for `ntlm.c`'s two static functions (`des_key_from_password`, `generate_lm_hash`), which are its only users.
